text: You can't always rely _____ other people to do the work for you.
note: Rely on (or depend on) someone or something.

text: Everyone in the village will benefit _____ the new health centre.
note: Benefit from something. (A benefit of something is the noun: the benefits of exercise.)

text: The new advertising campaign is aimed _____ teenagers.
note: Aim at / be aimed at a group of people or a target.

text: There is a serious lack _____ clean drinking water in the region.
note: A lack of something. The noun is followed by "of" (the verb is not: they lack experience).

text: The minister resigned _____ his position after the scandal.
note: Resign from a job or position. (Without an object: He resigned.)

text: Her skin is very sensitive _____ strong sunlight.
note: Sensitive to something (light, noise, criticism). Sensitive about = easily upset by a topic.

text: We should be more tolerant _____ people who think differently from us.
note: Tolerant of something or someone (also: tolerant towards people).

text: She seemed completely indifferent _____ the results of the election.
note: Indifferent to something = not interested in it.

text: Young children are often fascinated _____ dinosaurs.
note: Fascinated by (or with) something. Adjectives that describe a feeling caused by something often take "by": amazed by, shocked by.

text: Local residents are strongly opposed _____ the plan to build a new road.
note: Opposed to something. (We say "against" with other words: They voted against the plan.)

text: Your comments are not relevant _____ what we are discussing.
note: Relevant to something = connected with it.

text: He was completely unaware _____ the danger he was in.
note: Aware of / unaware of something.

text: Students under 26 are eligible _____ a reduced ticket price.
note: Eligible for something (a benefit, a prize). Eligible to + verb: eligible to vote.

text: After ten years abroad, she yearned _____ her home town.
note: Yearn for something = want it very much (long for).

text: On holiday, I like to indulge _____ a long, lazy breakfast.
note: Indulge in something = allow yourself to enjoy it.

text: My parents insisted _____ paying for the whole meal.
note: Insist on + -ing form (or on something).

text: I congratulated my brother _____ passing his driving test.
note: Congratulate someone on something.

text: The noise from the street prevented us _____ sleeping.
note: Prevent someone from + -ing form.

text: The committee consists _____ twelve members from different countries.
note: Consist of = be made up of. The verb is never used in a continuous tense.

text: He was accused _____ stealing money from the company.
note: Accuse someone of (doing) something. Compare: blame someone for something.

text: The manager blamed the delay _____ bad weather.
note: Blame something on a cause, or blame the cause for something: They blamed the weather for the delay.

text: She apologised _____ being late for the meeting.
note: Apologise for something you did. (You apologise to a person.)

text: It all depends _____ the weather.
note: Depend on something or someone.

text: After three attempts, he succeeded _____ passing the driving test.
note: Succeed in doing something. Followed by the -ing form.

text: I agree _____ you completely; it was a terrible idea.
note: Agree with a person or an opinion. (You agree on a plan, and agree to a request.)

text: Over 200 people participated _____ the survey.
note: Participate in an activity.

text: She doesn't really care _____ what other people think.
note: Care about something = think it is important.

text: I can't concentrate _____ my work with all this noise.
note: Concentrate on something.

text: Many people suffer _____ back pain at some point in their lives.
note: Suffer from an illness or a problem.

text: This book belongs _____ the school library.
note: Belong to someone or something.

text: She applied _____ a job at the local hospital.
note: Apply for a job, a place or a visa. (You apply to a company or a university.)

text: I'll pay _____ the tickets if you book the hotel.
note: Pay for something you buy.

text: We waited _____ the bus for half an hour.
note: Wait for someone or something.

text: Do you ever listen _____ classical music?
note: Listen to someone or something.

text: The other children laughed _____ his accent.
note: Laugh at someone or something = find it funny, often unkindly.

text: She's been married _____ a doctor for ten years.
note: Be married to someone.

text: Who is responsible _____ this mess?
note: Responsible for something that happened. (You are responsible to a person above you.)

text: They are very proud _____ their daughter.
note: Proud of someone or something.

text: Many people are afraid _____ spiders.
note: Afraid of something.

text: She's really good _____ maths and science.
note: Good at a subject or skill. (You are good with children or good for your health.)

text: I'm not very interested _____ football.
note: Interested in something.

text: Your idea is very similar _____ mine.
note: Similar to something.

text: She's worried _____ her exams next week.
note: Worried about something that might happen.

text: The children are really excited _____ the school trip.
note: Excited about something that is going to happen.

text: Paris is famous _____ its restaurants and museums.
note: Famous for something.

text: "He's late again." "That's typical _____ him!"
note: Typical of someone = what you would expect from them.

text: There has been a sharp increase _____ the price of fuel.
note: An increase in something (a change in size or amount). Compare: an increase of 5 per cent.

text: What was the reason _____ your decision to leave?
note: A reason for something.

text: We still haven't found a solution _____ the problem.
note: A solution to a problem.

text: Smoking is a major cause _____ lung cancer.
note: A cause of something bad. (We also say "a cause for concern".)

text: This is a good example _____ how not to behave.
note: An example of something.

text: What was her reaction _____ the news?
note: A reaction to something.

text: Pollution has a serious effect _____ children's health.
note: An effect on something.

text: My parents don't approve _____ my choice of friends.
note: Approve of something or someone.

text: She complained _____ the noise to the hotel manager.
note: Complain about something (to a person).

text: She referred _____ her notes several times during the talk.
note: Refer to something = look at it or mention it.

text: He's still recovering _____ his operation.
note: Recover from an illness or an operation.

text: We arrived _____ the station just in time to catch the train.
note: Arrive at a small place or a building; arrive in a city or country.

text: He spends a lot of money _____ clothes and shoes.
note: Spend money on something.

text: The police are searching _____ the missing child.
note: Search for someone or something you can't find.

text: It's rude to stare _____ people on the train.
note: Stare at someone or something.

text: It is time to dispose _____ these old computers.
note: Dispose of something = get rid of it.

text: All companies must comply _____ the new safety regulations.
note: Comply with a rule, law or request.

text: Elderly people are more susceptible _____ infection in winter.
note: Susceptible to something (an illness, flattery, pressure).

text: Small children are particularly vulnerable _____ abuse.
note: Vulnerable to something harmful.

text: Drivers are legally liable _____ any damage they cause.
note: Liable for something = legally responsible for it. (Liable to + verb = likely to: liable to change.)

text: The crowd was openly hostile _____ the speaker.
note: Hostile to (or towards) someone or something.

text: There is no point in dwelling _____ the past.
note: Dwell on something = keep thinking or talking about it. (Dwell in = live in, formal.)

text: The most senior judge presided _____ the trial.
note: Preside over a meeting, trial or ceremony.

text: The president officially resides _____ the capital, though he often travels.
note: Reside in a city or country (formal for "live").

text: Your age is irrelevant _____ whether you get the job.
note: Irrelevant to something.

text: The region is renowned _____ its excellent wines.
note: Renowned (or famous, known) for something. "As" is used for a role: renowned as a chef.

text: Children under five are exempt _____ the charge.
note: Exempt from something = free from a rule or payment.

text: The company specialises _____ medical equipment for hospitals.
note: Specialise in something.

text: The refugees had been deprived _____ their basic rights.
note: Deprive someone of something.

text: The film is based _____ a true story.
note: Be based on something.

text: A quiet room is more conducive _____ studying than a noisy cafe.
note: Conducive to something = helping it to happen.

text: The scandal eventually resulted _____ the minister's resignation.
note: Result in = cause. Result from = be caused by: His resignation resulted from the scandal.

text: Employees are entitled _____ four weeks' paid holiday a year.
note: Entitled to something.

text: She derives great pleasure _____ working in her garden.
note: Derive something from something.

text: You must adhere _____ the rules of the competition.
note: Adhere to a rule, plan or principle.

text: Lack of sleep contributes _____ many health problems.
note: Contribute to something = help to cause it.

text: He attributes his success _____ hard work and a little luck.
note: Attribute something to a cause.

text: She finally consented _____ the operation.
note: Consent to something = agree to it.

text: He was completely preoccupied _____ his own problems.
note: Preoccupied with something = thinking about it all the time.

text: He seemed oblivious _____ the noise around him.
note: Oblivious to something = not noticing it.

text: Be wary _____ strangers who offer you cheap deals.
note: Wary of something or someone = careful about them.

text: She felt apprehensive _____ the interview.
note: Apprehensive about something = worried about what might happen.

text: The United Nations refused to intervene _____ the dispute.
note: Intervene in a situation = become involved to change it.

text: Questions pertaining _____ the case will not be discussed.
note: Pertain to something = be about it.

text: She subscribes _____ several scientific magazines.
note: Subscribe to a magazine or a service.

text: Several people commented _____ the lack of information.
note: Comment on something.

text: She dotes _____ her grandchildren and spoils them.
note: Dote on someone = love them very much and show it.

text: The company capitalised _____ its rival's mistake.
note: Capitalise on something = use it to your advantage.

text: He dabbles _____ photography in his spare time.
note: Dabble in something = take part in it, but not seriously.

text: She revels _____ the attention she gets.
note: Revel in something = enjoy it very much.

text: The problem is rooted _____ poverty and lack of education.
note: Be rooted in something = have it as its origin.

text: She was so immersed _____ her book that she missed her stop.
note: Be immersed in something = be completely involved in it.

text: In many people's minds, Paris is synonymous _____ romance.
note: Synonymous with something = very closely connected with it.

text: He built his career at the expense _____ his health.
note: At the expense of something = causing harm to it.

text: The work must be carried out in accordance _____ the law.
note: In accordance with something = following it.

text: In view _____ the circumstances, the decision seems reasonable.
note: In view of something = because of it.

text: In the absence _____ any evidence, he was released.
note: In the absence of something = when it is not there.

text: With regard _____ your recent enquiry, we are pleased to inform you that...
note: With regard to something = about it (formal).

text: She got the job by virtue _____ her experience.
note: By virtue of something = because of it (formal).

text: People move to cities in pursuit _____ a better life.
note: In pursuit of something = trying to get it.

text: She stayed calm in the face _____ danger.
note: In the face of something = when dealing with it.

text: The book gives a fascinating insight _____ life in the 1950s.
note: An insight into something = a deeper understanding of it.

text: There is a serious shortage _____ nurses in the region.
note: A shortage of something.

text: He has an unhealthy obsession _____ his appearance.
note: An obsession with something.

text: Cycling is a healthy alternative _____ driving to work.
note: An alternative to something.

text: The company has shown a strong commitment _____ quality.
note: A commitment to something.

text: She longed _____ a quiet life in the countryside.
note: Long for something = want it very much.

text: Critics scoffed _____ the idea, but it worked.
note: Scoff at something = laugh at it in an unkind way.

text: She clung _____ the hope that he would come back.
note: Cling to something = refuse to let it go.

text: We tried to dissuade him _____ going out in the storm.
note: Dissuade someone from doing something = persuade them not to.

text: Several members decided to abstain _____ voting.
note: Abstain from something = choose not to do it.

text: Someone has tampered _____ the lock.
note: Tamper with something = change it without permission.

text: He panders _____ the voters' prejudices to win support.
note: Pander to someone = give them what they want, often something not good.

text: She has a real flair _____ languages.
note: A flair for something = a natural talent for it.

text: He has nothing but disdain _____ people who work for money.
note: Disdain for someone = a feeling that they are not good enough.

text: It is hard to reconcile his generous words _____ his selfish actions.
note: Reconcile one thing with another.

text: After weeks of pressure, she finally succumbed _____ temptation.
note: Succumb to something (temptation, pressure, an illness).

text: He seems quite incapable _____ telling the truth.
note: Capable of / incapable of (doing) something.

text: The low-lying fields are prone _____ flooding in spring.
note: Prone to something (usually bad) = likely to have or suffer it.

text: The report was bereft _____ any new ideas.
note: Bereft of something = completely without it (formal).

text: His speech was replete _____ references to ancient history.
note: Replete with something = full of it (formal).

text: She grew up in a family steeped _____ the traditions of the theatre.
note: Steeped in history or tradition = full of it, deeply influenced by it.

text: The government is answerable _____ parliament for its decisions.
note: Answerable to someone for something.

text: The prime minister seemed impervious _____ criticism.
note: Impervious to something = not affected by it.

text: After years in the Arctic, he was inured _____ the cold.
note: Inured to something unpleasant = used to it so it no longer affects you.

text: The collapse of the bridge was attributable _____ poor maintenance.
note: Attributable to a cause. Compare: attribute something to a cause.

text: His public statements are at odds _____ his private views.
note: At odds with something = in conflict with it.

text: She has harboured a grudge _____ her former boss ever since.
note: A grudge against someone.

text: He has a deep aversion _____ crowds.
note: An aversion to something = a strong dislike of it.

text: The sale is contingent _____ approval from the board.
note: Contingent on (or upon) something = depending on it.

text: At the age of twenty, she embarked _____ a career in journalism.
note: Embark on something new (a journey, a career, a project).

text: He was bent _____ revenge and would not listen to anyone.
note: Be bent on (doing) something = be determined to.

text: The whole theory is predicated _____ the assumption that prices will keep rising.
note: Be predicated on (or upon) something = be based on it.

text: The students showed an insatiable appetite _____ knowledge.
note: An appetite for something = a strong wish for it.

text: She took umbrage _____ the remark and left the room.
note: Take umbrage at something = be offended by it.

text: He is amenable _____ suggestions, so just ask him.
note: Amenable to something = willing to accept it.

text: He felt beholden _____ the sponsors who had paid for his studies.
note: Beholden to someone = owing them a favour.

text: The company is fully cognisant _____ the risks involved.
note: Cognisant of something = aware of it (formal).

text: She was accused of being complicit _____ the cover-up.
note: Complicit in something bad = involved in it.

text: The soil is deficient _____ nutrients.
note: Deficient in something = not having enough of it.

text: The whole speech was devoid _____ humour.
note: Devoid of something = completely without it.

text: Your point is not germane _____ the discussion.
note: Germane to something = relevant to it.

text: Such policies are inimical _____ economic growth.
note: Inimical to something = harmful to it.

text: Only a handful of officials were privy _____ the secret.
note: Privy to something = knowing a secret.

text: The smell was redolent _____ her grandmother's kitchen.
note: Redolent of something = bringing it to mind.

text: His actions were not consonant _____ his stated values.
note: Consonant with something = in agreement with it.

text: The new rules impinge _____ our freedom to choose.
note: Impinge on something = affect it in a way that limits it.

text: Developers have begun to encroach _____ the national park.
note: Encroach on something = slowly take more of it than is right.

text: The government finally acceded _____ the strikers' demands.
note: Accede to something = agree to it (formal).

text: Five teams are vying _____ the championship title.
note: Vie for something = compete to get it.

text: He was wallowing _____ self-pity after losing his job.
note: Wallow in something = enjoy or stay in a bad feeling.

text: The team was basking _____ the glory of their victory.
note: Bask in something = enjoy praise or attention.

text: All offers are subject _____ contract.
note: Subject to something = depending on it.

text: Her account is at variance _____ the evidence.
note: At variance with something = not agreeing with it.

text: The two agencies work in tandem _____ each other.
note: In tandem with something = working together with it.

text: The research was carried out in conjunction _____ the university.
note: In conjunction with something = together with it.

text: They changed the date in deference _____ her wishes.
note: In deference to someone = out of respect for them.

text: The country is in the throes _____ a political crisis.
note: In the throes of something = in the middle of a difficult process.

text: Scientists are on the cusp _____ a major discovery.
note: On the cusp of something = about to reach a new stage.

text: He worked long hours, to the detriment _____ his health.
note: To the detriment of something = causing harm to it.

text: The inquiry was set up at the behest _____ the prime minister.
note: At the behest of someone = because they ordered it.

text: The thieves were seen in the vicinity _____ the station.
note: In the vicinity of a place = near it.

text: She reached the top by dint _____ hard work.
note: By dint of something = by means of it.

text: He has a predilection _____ sweet foods.
note: A predilection for something = a strong liking for it.

text: She had no inkling _____ what was about to happen.
note: An inkling of something = a slight idea of it.

text: Such language is an affront _____ human dignity.
note: An affront to something = an insult to it.

text: The police restored a semblance _____ order.
note: A semblance of something = an appearance of it, often not complete.

text: He showed not a modicum _____ respect for her feelings.
note: A modicum of something = a small amount of it.

text: The website offers a plethora _____ options for travellers.
note: A plethora of something = a very large amount of it.

text: There is a dearth _____ qualified teachers in rural areas.
note: A dearth of something = a lack of it.

text: We are suffering from a surfeit _____ information and a shortage of time.
note: A surfeit of something = too much of it.

text: He pined _____ his lost love for years.
note: Pine for someone or something = long for them sadly.

text: The soldiers swore allegiance _____ the crown.
note: Allegiance to someone or something = loyalty to them.

text: A free press is a bulwark _____ tyranny.
note: A bulwark against something = a protection from it.

text: Swallows are a harbinger _____ spring.
note: A harbinger of something = a sign that it is coming.

text: The holiday gave her a welcome respite _____ the pressures of work.
note: A respite from something = a short rest from it.
